task.description:
REWORK ITERATION 1 OF 3 on Step 3's amendment (commit 131aba9). REVIEWER's Step 3b gate returned FAIL with 1 BLOCKER, 4 MAJOR and 3 MINOR. Read `handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json`'s `result.issues` in full — each finding names its measurement, its exact file/line, and a proposed FIX. This handoff is carried as its own file rather than by mutating step-03-amendment.json, so the record of what the first pass produced survives; ORCHESTRATOR.md §5's 'increment rework_count on the original handoff' would have overwritten it, and that drift is recorded, not silently resolved.

WHAT IS NOT IN QUESTION, so you do not undo it: gate checks (1), (3), (4) and (5) PASSED and re-derivations (i), (iii), (iv), (v), (vi) all confirmed. All four ISS-0117 questions are genuinely decided — including Q4 decided AGAINST the issue's own framing, which is correct. The instruction-precedence nil result was independently reproduced over a WIDER file set than you used. The §5 rework-counter scoping is loophole-free. Append-only, §7.1 and §6 are intact. **No decision needs re-taking. Every finding below is a text correction inside the two files you already own.**

MUST FIX — BLOCKER-1. The measurement justifying the required-field-over-convention decision is wrong, in two places, and each sentence is contradicted by its own parenthetical. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md ~line 260 says 'five occurrences across four runs, under three different ad-hoc top-level key names (orch_restart_note, orch_timestamp_correction ×2, orch_reconstruction)' — the parenthetical enumerates FOUR. Line ~394 repeats it. MEASURED by REVIEWER over all 547 handoff files, and independently re-derived by ORCH: there are FOUR occurrences of an ad-hoc recovery key, in FOUR files, in FOUR runs (WF02-REQ023, WF02-REQ027, WF02-REQ037, WF03-ISS0109). The fifth incident is WF02-REQ043-20260818, which carries NO key at all — it is the UNREPAIRED counter-example §4.1(a-2) cites, so it is not an instance of the convention. SECOND ERROR, same paragraph: 'changed shape from a bare string to a structured object between its FIRST AND SECOND use', closed by 'A convention that changed shape on its second application is not a convention.' Sorted by completed_at the four uses are REQ023 18:49:40Z string, REQ027 21:35:39Z string, REQ037 (2026-08-17) string, ISS0109 (2026-08-21) object — the object appears on the FOURTH use, five days and three string-shaped uses after the first. The rhetorical close rests on a wrong ordinal. FIX: state the measured figures — four occurrences, four runs, three key names, two key positions (18/18 and 11/18), two shapes with the object on the fourth and most recent use — and if the five-incident frequency is still wanted, say it SEPARATELY as five death incidents across five runs, four of which improvised a key. Rewrite the closing line so it rests on the true ordinal; 'three string-shaped uses over five days, then an object' is a stronger argument than the wrong one it replaces. THE DECISION THE NUMBERS SUPPORT IS UNAFFECTED — only the numbers are wrong. Note why this is a BLOCKER rather than a MINOR: it is the FOURTH firing of docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source', occurring INSIDE the amendment that warns about it, and the next agent inherits the misquote.

MUST FIX — MAJOR-1 (check 7). §2's schema block was VALID, machine-parseable JSON before your commit and is not after it. ORCH verified this independently: extracting the first ```json fence and running json.loads gives '131aba9^ -> PARSES, 17 top-level keys' and '131aba9 -> PARSE ERROR: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 48 column 3'. Your own MINOR justified the `//` comments on the premise that the block was already unparseable because of placeholders — that premise is measurably false: `<uuid-v4>`, `<AGENT_ID>` and `<ISO8601-UTC or null>` are all INSIDE double-quoted strings and are legal JSON, which is exactly why it parsed. A schema block agents read as a contract lost machine-readability, on a false premise, in the same amendment arguing its own rule is worth having because it is greppable and lintable and naming `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` as the enforcement surface. FIX: move the three `//` lines out of the fence into a prose paragraph immediately beneath it, keeping the field itself inside the block. Restores parseability with no loss of visibility, and CLOSES the MINOR rather than recording it.

MUST FIX — MAJOR-2 (check 2). §3's exception column sends THREE fields to §4.1 — `completed_at`, `status`, `result` — but §4.1(a-2)'s normative text authorises exactly one: 'So ORCH, and only ORCH, writes the `result` block.' ORCH's authority over `completed_at` and over setting `status` appears nowhere as a rule; it survives only as an illustrative value inside §4.1(b)'s `fields_written` row. This is the precise drift check (2) exists to catch — a pointer stated in one section whose target is incomplete in the other — and it matters twice: (a) the amendment's own motivating incident IS ORCH writing `completed_at` without declaring it, so the field whose undeclared reconstruction prompted the rule is the one the exception clause never licenses; (b) a weak model reading §4.1(a-2) literally writes `result` and leaves `status` PENDING with `completed_at` null, reproducing WF02-REQ043's defect that the paragraph three lines above rejects by measurement. FIX: in §4.1(a-2), state the three fields ORCH writes and that all three must appear in `fields_written`, so each of §3's three pointers lands on explicit text.

MUST FIX — MAJOR-3 (check 2). §4.1's ISS-0192 parenthetical misstates its own cited source and would invert the field's meaning if followed. It claims §4.1 governs the later repair of BOTH WF02-REQ043 and WF02-REQ062. docs/issues/ISS-0192.yaml says the opposite of the second: WF02-REQ062-20260819/step-03-test-designer.json is NOT agent death — TEST-DESIGNER performed §4's steps 2 and 3 and skipped step 1, and it carries a full agent-written result with status PASS and a real completed_at. Applying §4.1(a-2) would have ORCH stamp `not_agent_attested` onto a result the acting agent DID attest — asserting the exact falsehood the field exists to prevent. FIX: scope the parenthetical to WF02-REQ043 only, and add one clause saying WF02-REQ062 is a plain §4 step-1 omission outside §4.1's class. ALSO, same paragraph pair (REVIEWER's related MINOR): WF02-REQ043 is cited as the (a-2) reconstruct exemplar AND as the mid-action (a-1) exemplar. Both are true at different times — mid-action at death, side effects complete today — but the document never says so. Add one clause noting that (c)'s classification is evaluated AT REPAIR TIME, not at death time, which the predicate rule already implies and ISS-0192 is about to depend on.

MUST FIX — MAJOR-4 (check 6). Optional-by-absence is unsound as written, and its failure is already on disk. §4.1(b) states unconditionally that 'absence asserts that the result is the acting agent's own report'. But 546 handoff files predate this rule and none were audited, so absence in them means 'the rule did not exist yet'. Worse, it is not theoretical: WF03-ISS0109's step-final IS a reconstruction, carries `orch_reconstruction` rather than `not_agent_attested`, and §4.1(b) forbids backfilling it — so `grep -rl not_agent_attested handoffs/`, the command §4.1(b) offers as the field's ENTIRE justification, returns ZERO reconstructions in a repository containing exactly one, permanently. FIX, both parts needed: (1) date-scope the assertion — absence carries the attestation claim only for handoffs created on or after this rule's date, and files predating it are explicitly unaudited. One sentence, and it makes the greppability claim honest. (2) Name the WF03-ISS0109 file as the SINGLE exception to no-backfill: renaming its `orch_reconstruction` to `not_agent_attested` and adding `fields_written: ["status","completed_at","result"]` is a key rename over evidence already present and already ORCH's own — not a retro-fitted claim, which is what the no-backfill rationale rightly forbids in general. NOTE: you are authorising that backfill in the text; do NOT perform it — the file belongs to another run, and ORCH will route it.

RIDE-ALONG — MINOR-1 (check 2), modality drift. §2's comment says 'present ONLY on a handoff recovered under §4.1' while §4.1(a-1) says a redispatch writes NO marker. Read strictly §2 is true, but a weak model reading the schema block alone can take 'recovered under §4.1' to include (a-1) and stamp the field onto a replacement agent's genuine first-hand report. FIX: 'present ONLY on a handoff reconstructed under §4.1(a-2); a §4.1(a-1) redispatch does not carry it.' (REVIEWER confirmed all six member names match §4.1(b)'s table exactly, in order — do not disturb that.)

RIDE-ALONG — MINOR-2 (check ii/6), stale headcount. §4.1(b) says 'All 534 handoff files currently in handoffs/ remain valid unchanged.' Measured at your own commit: 547 json files, i.e. 546 handoffs plus registry.json. 534 was accurate about three hours earlier. The deeper problem is the shape, not the value: a monotonically growing count written into a protocol as a fixed figure is wrong again by the next run. FIX: drop the number, or write 'every handoff file predating this rule', which is what the sentence means.

OUT OF SCOPE — MINOR-3. ORCHESTRATOR.md's absence from core-directives.md's precedence chain is real and is being filed by ORCH as its own issue. Do NOT fix it here and do NOT edit core-directives.md.

CONSTRAINTS UNCHANGED: write ONLY to docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md. Do not edit docs/issues/*.yaml, do not repair any other run's handoff files, do not touch registry.json or orchestrator.log, no code, no tests. Do not call gh or the queue; report anything needing an id in result.issues.

CHANGE-APPROACH NOTE per ORCHESTRATOR.md §5: the root cause of BLOCKER-1 and MINOR-2 is the same — figures were carried over from the Step 1 diagnosis instead of re-derived. So for this pass, RE-RUN the counts yourself and quote the commands, rather than copying any number from REVIEWER's findings either. REVIEWER's figures are a record too.
acceptance_criteria: BLOCKER-1 fixed in BOTH places (~line 260 and ~line 394): the occurrence count, run count, key-position and shape-ordinal figures all match a count re-derived in THIS pass, with the command quoted in result.summary; the five-incident frequency, if retained, is stated separately and distinctly from the four-key count
The closing rhetorical line no longer rests on 'second application' or any other unmeasured ordinal

MAJOR-1 fixed: the first ```json fence in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md parses under `json.loads` — verified in this pass with the command and its output quoted — and the field remains inside the block with its explanation as prose beneath

MAJOR-2 fixed: §4.1(a-2) explicitly names `result`, `status` and `completed_at` as the fields ORCH writes, and requires all three in `fields_written`; each of §3's three exception pointers now lands on explicit normative text

MAJOR-3 fixed: the ISS-0192 parenthetical is scoped to WF02-REQ043 only, WF02-REQ062 is named as outside §4.1's class, and a clause states that (c)'s classification is evaluated at repair time rather than at death time

MAJOR-4 fixed: the absence-carries-attestation claim is date-scoped, pre-rule files are explicitly unaudited, and the WF03-ISS0109 file is named in the text as the single no-backfill exception — WITHOUT that file being edited by this step
MINOR-1 and MINOR-2 fixed; the six member names in §2 still match §4.1(b)'s table exactly and in order
Gate checks (1), (3), (4), (5) and re-derivations (i), (iii), (iv), (v), (vi) are NOT disturbed — no decision re-taken, no passing text rewritten beyond what these findings require
Every figure now appearing in either file was re-derived in this pass, not copied from the Step 1 diagnosis or from REVIEWER's findings; result.summary says which commands produced them
`git status --porcelain` shows changes confined to the two owned files plus this handoff; the output is quoted

result.summary:
Rework iteration 1 of 3 complete. All 8 findings in scope addressed (BLOCKER-1, MAJOR-1..4, MINOR-1, MINOR-2, plus one stale figure found by my own re-derivation); MINOR-3 left untouched as instructed. Only docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md were written. No decision re-taken: gate checks (1),(3),(4),(5) and re-derivations (i),(iii),(iv),(v),(vi) were not disturbed -- I did not touch the four-questions text, the S5 rework-counter paragraph, the ISS-0033 reconciliation in ORCHESTRATOR S7.2, or S5/S6/S7.1's append-only and detector rules.

=== EVERY FIGURE RE-DERIVED IN THIS PASS, WITH THE COMMAND ===
None were copied from the Step 1 diagnosis or from REVIEWER's findings.

(1) AD-HOC KEY COUNT. Script: json.load over all files matching handoffs/**/*.json (549 files = 1 registry.json + 548 handoffs, 0 unparseable), subtracting S2's 17 schema keys. Raw: 26 non-schema key occurrences in 13 files. Filtered to the recovery/correction class (the orch_* keys): FOUR, in FOUR files, in FOUR runs, sorted by completed_at:
  2026-08-16T18:49:40Z WF02-REQ023-20260816  orch_timestamp_correction str  pos 18/18
  2026-08-16T21:35:39Z WF02-REQ027-20260816  orch_restart_note         str  pos 18/18
  2026-08-17T19:45:30Z WF02-REQ037-20260817  orch_timestamp_correction str  pos 11/18
  2026-08-21T03:29:36Z WF03-ISS0109-20260821 orch_reconstruction       dict pos 18/18
So 4 occurrences, 4 files, 4 runs, 3 key names, 2 positions (18/18 x3, 11/18 x1), 2 shapes, object on the FOURTH and most recent use. Shape ordinal re-derived: three string uses inside 25 hours (08-16T18:49:40Z -> 08-17T19:45:30Z), then an object three days later (08-21T03:29:36Z).

(2) A FINDING BEYOND REVIEWER'S -- the 'five death incidents' fallback is ALSO wrong, so I did not adopt it. I read the four key VALUES rather than counting their names. WF02-REQ023's orch_timestamp_correction is ORCH correcting its own EXTRAPOLATED created_at/started_at; WF02-REQ037's is ORCH correcting SECURITY-REVIEWER's implausible completed_at. Neither is an agent ceasing to exist. Command: grep -rniE 'power outage|session limit|api error|terminated mid|died|agent death' handoffs/registry.json handoffs/orchestrator.log docs/issues/ISS-0117.yaml docs/issues/ISS-0192.yaml docs/issues/ISS-0046.yaml. Agent deaths actually evidenced: THREE, in THREE runs -- WF02-REQ027 (infra session limit; registry.json:273, orchestrator.log:223), WF02-REQ043 (host power outage mid-rebase; registry.json:856, corroborated by ISS-0046 and ISS-0192), WF03-ISS0109 (API error after the merge landed; ISS-0117.yaml:12 and the file's own orch_reconstruction.reason). S4.1's opening now states three-across-three with an incident table, and explicitly warns against conflating that set with S3's four keys.

(3) JSON FENCE PARSEABILITY (MAJOR-1). Command: extract the first json fence by regex and json.loads it, at three revisions. 131aba9^ -> PARSES, 17 top-level keys. 131aba9 -> PARSE ERROR: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 48 column 3 (char 1672). Independently confirms REVIEWER and refutes the premise my previous pass used. AFTER THIS PASS: WORKTREE -> PARSES, 18 top-level keys; not_agent_attested's members are ['reconstructed_by','reconstructed_at','reason','fields_written','evidence','not_verifiable_after_the_fact'] -- identical, same order, to S4.1(b)'s table (verified at lines 438-443).

(4) STATUS ENUM VIOLATIONS. Same scan: 13 files carry an out-of-enum top-level status, all 'PASS' (11 in WF02-REQ063-20260818, plus WF02-REQ064-20260818 step-01 and step-02a); 2 more (WF02-REQ059/REQ060 step-00-git-setup.json) have no top-level status key at all. 13 + 2 = 15. Both figures reproduce; the text now states both halves explicitly and dates the measurement.

(5) e25822a. git log --oneline -1 e25822a -> 'e25822a feat(WF02-REQ043): instance-engine schema -- instance_projections ALTER, tokens, tasks (#174)'; git merge-base --is-ancestor e25822a main -> true. Used for the new repair-time clause.

(6) ISS-0192's TWO FILES. WF02-REQ043 step-final: status='PENDING', completed_at=None, result=None. WF02-REQ062 step-03: status='PENDING', completed_at='2026-08-19T05:25:43Z', result.status='PASS'. Confirms the second is NOT this section's class.

(7) grep -rl not_agent_attested handoffs/ -> orchestrator.log plus this run's four WF03-ISS0117 handoff files ONLY. WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json is absent, so the enumeration command returns zero of the one reconstruction that exists. MAJOR-4 confirmed on disk.

(8) A STALE FIGURE I FOUND MYSELF, not in REVIEWER's findings. ORCHESTRATOR.md S7.2 said last_known_step is 'Used 64 times in handoffs/registry.json'. git show 131aba9:handoffs/registry.json | grep -c '"last_known_step"' -> 62; at HEAD -> 62; worktree -> 63. Wrong when written AND a growing count, i.e. exactly MINOR-2's shape in the other owned file. Replaced with 'nearly every run entry' plus a note recording the measured discrepancy.

=== WHAT CHANGED, FINDING BY FINDING ===
BLOCKER-1 -- fixed in BOTH places. S3 (was ~line 260) now carries a four-row measured table (key/run/completed_at/shape/position) and states 4 occurrences / 4 files / 4 runs / 3 names / 2 positions / 2 shapes, distinguishing the two timestamp-correction cases from the two death cases. S4.1(b) (was ~line 394) no longer restates a count that contradicts its own parenthetical; it points at S3's table and spends its words on the shape ORDINAL. The closing line no longer says 'second application' or 'five agents': it now reads that the string shape held long enough for two later writers to reproduce it and was then silently replaced by a fourth. The five-incident frequency is NOT retained in the four-key form; S4.1's opening states the death incidents separately as three-across-three with an explicit do-not-conflate sentence, because re-deriving showed 'five deaths' is unsupportable too.
MAJOR-1 -- fixed. The three // lines are out of the fence; not_agent_attested stays inside the block. A prose paragraph beneath the fence carries the explanation and states the block is machine-parseable and must stay so. Verified: json.loads succeeds, 18 keys. The MINOR is CLOSED, not re-recorded.
MAJOR-2 -- fixed. S4.1(a-2) now reads 'ORCH, and only ORCH, completes the handoff' and enumerates the three fields as a numbered list -- status, completed_at (fresh clock read at repair time, never back-dated), result -- requires all three in fields_written, names the PENDING/null failure mode it prevents, and states started_at is NOT on the list. S3's three exception pointers each now land on explicit normative text.
MAJOR-3 -- fixed. The ISS-0192 parenthetical is scoped to WF02-REQ043 alone. WF02-REQ062 gets its own paragraph naming it a plain S4 step-1 omission outside this section's class, quoting its measured status/completed_at/result.status, and stating that stamping the field on it would assert the falsehood the field prevents. Added the discriminator that was missing: a null result puts a handoff in this class, a bare PENDING does not. The repair-time clause is added in (c), naming WF02-REQ043 on both sides with e25822a as the evidence.
MAJOR-4 -- fixed, both parts. (1) The assertion is date-scoped to 2026-08-21: on-or-after, absence asserts agent attestation; before, absence asserts nothing, because those files were never audited against a rule that did not exist. (2) The WF03-ISS0109 file is named in the text as the single authorised backfill, with the rename and the fields_written value spelled out and the reason it is not a retro-fitted claim. The text says explicitly that this amendment does NOT perform it and that ORCH routes it. THE FILE WAS NOT TOUCHED -- it does not appear in git status.
MINOR-1 -- fixed. S2's prose says present ONLY on a handoff RECONSTRUCTED under S4.1(a-2), and that an (a-1) redispatch does not carry it, with the reason. Member names and order undisturbed.
MINOR-2 -- fixed. '534' is gone; the sentence reads 'every handoff file predating this rule', with a parenthetical saying the headcount was omitted deliberately because it grows every run.
MINOR-3 -- NOT touched. core-directives.md not edited.

The two doc files and this handoff are mine. orchestrator.log, registry.json and the four ISS-*.yaml are ORCH's own dispatch-time writes, left untouched and NOT staged or committed by me. No gh call, no queue call, no docs/issues edit, no other run's handoff file touched, no code, no tests. Residual-stale-figure sweep over both owned files: grep -nE '534|five occurrences|second use|second application|Used 64|across four runs|Five such' -> no matches.

issues.description: REPORTED, NOT ACTED ON -- needs an id from ORCH. REVIEWER's proposed fallback wording for BLOCKER-1 ('five death incidents across five runs, four of which improvised a key') does not survive re-derivation either, and I did not adopt it. Reading the four ad-hoc keys' VALUES rather than counting their names shows WF02-REQ023's and WF02-REQ037's orch_timestamp_correction are ORCH correcting extrapolated/implausible TIMESTAMPS, not agent deaths. Evidenced deaths are three, in three runs (WF02-REQ027 session limit, WF02-REQ043 power outage, WF03-ISS0109 API error). The 'five' figure therefore originated in the Step 1 diagnosis and passed through my Step 3 amendment AND through REVIEWER's own corrective finding without any of the three re-deriving it -- a further firing of docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source', and the first in which a GATE handoff was the carrier. Worth an anti-patterns.md addendum stating that a validator's corrective figure is itself a record. I did not edit anti-patterns.md: it is outside this handoff's two-file scope.

FIXED HERE, recorded because my own sweep found it rather than the gate. docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md S7.2 stated last_known_step is 'Used 64 times in handoffs/registry.json'. Measured: 62 at 131aba9, 62 at HEAD, 63 in the worktree -- wrong when written, and a monotonically growing count, i.e. the same defect shape as MINOR-2 in the other owned file. ORCH is filing this separately; restated only so it is not lost between handoffs.

Ask it to re-derive S3's ad-hoc-key table and S4.1's three-death table independently, since I corrected BOTH the amendment's original figure AND the replacement figure REVIEWER proposed -- the three-death count is new in this pass and has not been through any gate.
